messages:
maria: Heads-up — we need a follow-up decision on the control-plane <-> runtime abstraction for hosted/dedicated/private. Current problem: too many ad-hoc shims in adapters and ops is juggling fallbacks that leak tenant expectations.
aj: can you scope the decision? is this about auth + routing only or include telemetry/rollouts?
maria: mostly auth/routing and capability discovery. but rollout behavior (canary, fallback) needs a clear default. ops wants a single predictable policy rather than per-adapter heuristics.
devin: TL;DR: propose a small capability contract + opt-in routing policies. adapters must advertise a minimal surface: supported models, max_seq_len, quantization_levels, regional_tags, and whether they support prefix/KV cache. then control plane can route or fall back with confidence.
samir: +1. also important: define authority for tenant isolation decisions. who enforces tenant quotas? runtime or control-plane? My vote: runtime enforces strict isolation (cgroup-level, kms scoping), control-plane issues tokens and scopes only. This prevents silent over-commit.
aj: question: how do we version capability schema? we don't want forever-breaking adapters.
elaine: proposal: capability vector with a stable v1 shape. example: ```
capabilities_v1: [
  {"name": "models", "values": ["redwood-alpha", "llama-2-70b"]},
  {"name": "kv_cache", "values": ["prefix", "none"]},
  {"name": "quant", "values": ["fp16", "int8"]},
  {"name": "routing_weight", "values": ["hot", "cold"]}
]
```
This is illustrative; real payload will be compact and typed. Backwards compat: unknown keys are ignored, new enum values appended.
maria: good. follow-up: what happens when control-plane tries to route to an adapter that claims model but runtime actually can't serve that precision or seq len? we need a health/validation handshake.
devin: add a lightweight validation check at deploy time + a dynamic health probe endpoint. On mismatch, runtime should return a structured error with hinting: `supported_seq_max=4096, requested=8192` so control plane can fallback to compatible variant or reject with clear message.
samir: also record those mismatches in telemetry and surface as regression alerts in Optimize.
aj: does this change our token issuance? e.g., hosted tokens vs dedicated tokens must carry different claims.
elaine: yes: tokens issued by control-plane include `env` claim (hosted/dedicated/private), optional `tenant_policy` hash, and `capability_allowlist` for dedicated/private when enterprises need stricter scoping. runtime MUST refuse tokens without matching `env`.
maria: question about rollouts: can we do canary across environments? e.g., send 5% to dedicated variant then fallback to hosted?
devin: technically yes if adapter advertises `cross_env_fallback=true` and the tenant permits. But for security/regulatory reasons, default is no cross-env routing unless explicitly enabled for the tenant. add an org-level flag.
aj: sounds reasonable. concerns: complexity in ops UI to control per-tenant flags.
elaine: UX note — expose a single toggle in Console with an audit trail. default off. logging: every cross-env decision must be a trace event with reason code.
maria: implement plan: 1) define capability v1 spec (small doc) 2) add `/capabilities` discovery endpoint + `/validate` for deploy-time check, 3) require structured error codes for capability mismatches, 4) extend token claims with `env` and `capability_allowlist`, 5) default cross-env routing disabled and opt-in per-org.
samir: +1. timeline?
maria: devs: can you draft the capability schema + example validation responses by EOD Friday?
devin: I can take schema. will post PR: 1970.
aj: I'll prototype the token claim acceptance flow and a runtime flag.
elaine: I'll wire Console toggle and audit log entry design.
deploy-bot: deploy: feature/capability-discovery spec pushed to staging at 1969999000 — check `capabilities-v1.md` in the spec repo. :rocket:
maria: thanks team. we'll sync Friday 1pm to sign-off. If anyone sees a major blocker (regulatory/enterprise legal) raise it here before noon. :thumbsup:
